title: W2 GQR eligible-circle span and Frobenius-pair completion reduction

theorem.statement: For every odd prime p, the binary incidence words of nonsquare Miquelian circles meeting {infinity,0} in 0 or 2 points span H0 intersect ker(e_infinity+e_0), of dimension (p^2-1)/2.
proof_route: A same-type tangent pencil sums to the all-ones word.
A tangent pencil with exactly two edge-incompatible circles identifies their classes modulo the eligible-circle span.
The bipartite tangency graph is a Cayley graph on M=(F_{p^2}^*)^2 with connection set {(1+r sigma)^(-2): r in F_p}.
If the connection set failed to generate M, a nontrivial even character eta of F_(p^2)^* would equal one on an affine F_p-line.

Parameterising that line by the norm-one torus converts its character sum to Katz's t=-2 Soto-Andrade sum. The two exceptional character pairs both induce trivial eta, so the 2 sqrt(p) bound applies and contradicts a sum of p for p>=5; p=3 is direct.
All edge-incompatible circle generators therefore have one quotient class, which cancels in every edge-even codeword.

circle_completion.criterion: A Max-minus vector y can be flipped on a nonsquare circle S and remain Max-minus iff y restricted to S equals plus or minus the unique signed sparse -p eigenvector v_S.

oeis_web.note: Returned matches were unrelated numerical coincidences (for example semiprimes and linear sequences).

backend: Small exact ranks and p=5,7 scans on soulkiller; full p=11 data-local scan plus p=19 HiGHS/CP-SAT on NUKA; no process left running.
note: This proves the linear circle-code half and isolates a factor-degree-free nonlinear completion lemma. W2 remains OPEN.
